title: WHO pandemic agreement: PABS annex negotiations

charter.in: WHO member states' negotiations on the Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) annex to the WHO Pandemic Agreement adopted in 2025: the rules for sharing pathogen samples and sequence data and the vaccines, tests and treatments that result. The agreement cannot open for signature until the annex is finished. Stories on the talks' progress, deadlines, extensions, divisions and appeals to finish them belong; covered from January 2026.
out: The UN General Assembly political declaration on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response (September-October 2026)
The 2025 adoption of the Pandemic Agreement itself and the International Health Regulations amendments, except as the starting point of these talks
US bilateral health deals that demand pathogen samples or data from African countries
WHO preparedness and surveillance initiatives (24-hour detection target, Pandemic Fund, BioHub)
Outbreaks themselves (Ebola/Bundibugyo, hantavirus) and general warnings about outbreak risk
Wildlife trade and pathogen spillover research
US biosecurity policy and AI-enabled pathogen design
charter.endEvent: The World Health Assembly adopts the PABS annex, so the Pandemic Agreement can open for signature (or the talks are formally abandoned). Our stories put the target first at the May 2026 Assembly, then at May 2027.

notes: Not closed: no story reports the annex adopted, and the 26 Sep story gives May 2027 as the new target. The hardest call is '124 countries back new global health rules' (2 Nov). Its text reports the World Health Assembly adopting the Pandemic Agreement itself (124 in favor and none against in the committee vote, more WHO funding, the US absent from the final talks). Its source is CIDRAP's article 'World Health Assembly adopts Pandemic Agreement', and our 31 Jan and 8 Feb stories date that adoption to 2025. The story itself says countries 'still need to negotiate a system for sharing pathogens and benefits before the agreement can open for signature'. So it is neither the PABS end event nor the International Health Regulations amendments. It is a late re-report of the parent treaty's founding vote, and it must not close this development; its 124 is the vote on the main agreement, not on the annex. It is optional, not a near miss, because it is the same agreement and states the annex's status, but it adds no news about the talks, and putting it on a 2 Nov timeline as 'adopted' would mislead. The UN high-level-meeting stories split two ways. 26 Sep and 28 Sep are optional (26 Sep carries the May 2027 target; 28 Sep is a WHO call to 'complete' the pact). 29 Sep and 13 Oct are near misses about the UN political declaration. Figures are []: no number about the talks appears in 3 entries. The 10% donation and 10% WHO reserve appear only on 12 Sep and 124 only on 2 Nov; COVID's toll ('up to twenty million lives', 'more than 20 million excess deaths') is context, not a tracked figure.
